# Results — Study 381 (TIPS-Breakeven)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The bond market's **breakeven
inflation rate** — the market-implied inflation forecast — tested as a tradable macro timing
signal on a **transparent proxy**. True breakeven (FRED `T10YIE`) is not reliably fetchable
here, so we construct it from yfinance ETFs: the breakeven proxy is **`be = log(TIP / IEF)`**
(inflation-protected over duration-matched nominal Treasuries), which rises with the
market-implied inflation forecast. We test its **level** (expanding z-score) and **3-month
change** against forward 3/6/12-month returns of TIPS (`TIP`), equities (`SPY`) and gold
(`GLD`) with HAC (Newey-West) predictive-regression *t*-stats, a placebo null, win-rates and a
traded sign rule. Offline & deterministic; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every
number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted closes — `TIP`, `IEF`, `SPY`, `GLD` (public, no key) |
| Window | 2004-11-18 → 2026-06-18 (**5,429** trading days; **21.6** years; common to all four ETFs, GLD-limited) |
| Signal cadence | **260** month-ends; breakeven proxy = **`log(TIP/IEF)`**, **PROXY** for FRED `T10YIE` |
| Signals | **level-z** (expanding z-score, ≥24 obs, no look-ahead) and **3m-change** (trailing 3-month Δ) |
| Inference | OLS predictive regression with a **Newey-West HAC** *t* (Bartlett, bandwidth = horizon), placebo null |
| Entry / costs | 1-month execution lag; 10 bps one-way × monthly turnover on the traded sign rule |

> **Proxy caveat (named on the Signal axis).** `log(TIP/IEF)` is a *return-space* stand-in for
> the literal nominal-minus-real yield breakeven. It tracks the same object (it co-moves with
> `T10YIE`), but because it is built **from TIP**, any test that asks it to predict forward
> *TIP* returns is partly predicting the signal's own mean reversion — a mechanical
> autocorrelation, not a macro edge. We therefore read the TIP column with that asterisk and
> weight the genuinely independent targets (SPY, GLD). The verdict does not hinge on the
> proxy's exact construction: it hinges on the fact that no honest, *independent*,
> multiple-testing-aware edge survives.

## The signal — HAC predictive-regression scan (18 tests)

Slope and Newey-West *t* of forward `h`-month asset return on the breakeven signal; placebo *p*
is `P[|t| of a circularly-shuffled signal ≥ |t| observed]` (5,000 draws).

| signal | asset | h | slope | NW *t* | placebo *p* | n |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| level-z | **TIP** | 3 | −0.0045 | **−2.40** | 0.11 | 234 |
| level-z | **TIP** | 6 | −0.0081 | **−2.19** | 0.13 | 231 |
| level-z | **TIP** | 12 | −0.0142 | **−2.00** | 0.16 | 225 |
| 3m-change | TIP | 12 | −0.3907 | −1.90 | 0.14 | 245 |
| level-z | SPY | 12 | −0.0126 | −0.63 | 0.54 | 225 |
| 3m-change | SPY | 3 | +0.4842 | +1.29 | 0.28 | 254 |
| level-z | GLD | 12 | +0.0268 | +0.81 | 0.58 | 225 |
| 3m-change | **GLD** | 3 | −0.6067 | **−3.21** | **0.01** | 254 |
| 3m-change | GLD | 12 | −0.7317 | −1.41 | 0.22 | 245 |

*(The remaining nine cells — TIP/3m-change 3m & 6m, SPY level-z 3m & 6m, SPY 3m-change 6m & 12m,
GLD level-z 3m & 6m, GLD 3m-change 6m — all sit at `|t| < 1.4`. Full 18-row table in
`verify.py`.)*

**Read it carefully.** Across the **18** signal × asset × horizon tests, **3** cross `|t| ≥ 2`
— but at the 5% level you expect ~0.9 by chance, and the placebo null demotes most of them:

- The two **TIP/level-z** hits (`t = −2.40 / −2.19 / −2.00`) are a **mechanical artifact**. The
  breakeven proxy is built from TIP, so "high breakeven ⇒ TIP underperforms" is just the
  proxy **mean-reverting**: the breakeven level predicts its *own* forward 6-month change at
  `t = −1.98`. Under the honest placebo null these "hits" sit at `p ≈ 0.11–0.16` — **not
  significant**. You cannot trade "the signal will revert" as a macro edge.
- On **equities (SPY)** — the asset the folklore most wants to time — **nothing** is robust at
  any horizon (`|t| ≤ 1.3`).
- The single hit on a genuinely independent asset is **GLD / 3m-change at 3 months**
  (`t = −3.21`, placebo `p = 0.01`). It is exactly the **1-in-18 multiple-testing false
  positive** you'd expect — it does not survive at 6m (`t = −1.38`) or 12m (`t = −1.41`), and
  (below) it makes **negative money** as a strategy.

## Direction & costs — the one "hit" is a mirage as a trade

Directional win-rate (signed trade) vs the unconditional base rate; traded sign rule with a
1-month execution lag and 10 bps one-way × turnover.

| test | cond. win-rate | base win-rate |
|---|--:|--:|
| TIP level-z (12m) | 66% | 75% |
| SPY level-z (12m) | 68% | 83% |
| GLD 3m-change (3m) | 52% | 61% |

Every conditional win-rate is **below** its base rate — the signal subtracts from a naive long.
Now trade them:

| traded rule (sign, contrarian) | gross | net @10 bps | net Sharpe | buy-and-hold | B&H Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| GLD on 3m-change | −0.6%/yr | **−1.3%/yr** | −0.07 | **+11.4%/yr** | 0.67 |
| TIP on level-z | +1.9%/yr | +1.8%/yr | +0.32 | +3.5%/yr | 0.62 |

The "significant" `t = −3.21` gold regression turns into a **−1.3%/yr** money-loser versus
**+11.4%/yr** for simply holding gold — a textbook in-sample-*t* / out-of-sample-nothing mirage.
The TIP timer "works" only because it harvests the proxy's own mean reversion, and even then it
**underperforms buy-and-hold** (+1.8% vs +3.5%/yr) on a noisier ride.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful, and the null is a true null

Deterministic breakeven + asset series where next-month return is `μ + edge·z + noise` (`z` =
prior-month breakeven z-score). With the planted `edge = 0` the inference must find nothing;
with a large `edge` it must light up.

| planted edge | n | slope | NW *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.00** (no edge) | 216 | −0.0010 | **−0.37** | 0.68 |
| **+0.03** (large edge) | 216 | +0.0234 | **+7.93** | 0.00 |

With **no** planted edge the HAC *t* is `−0.37` (the test does **not** invent significance);
plant a real predictive slope and `t` jumps to `+7.93`. The control proves two things at once:
the measurement engine is unbiased, **and** the real-tape failure to find a robust independent
edge is a *true* null, not an underpowered one (260 months is plenty of power when the edge is
real).

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** The breakeven proxy does co-move with assets, and a couple of regressions
  cross `|t| = 2` — but the only ones that do are a **mechanical self-prediction** of TIPS
  (the proxy mean-reverting, placebo `p ≈ 0.11–0.16`) and a **single 1-in-18 gold false
  positive** that vanishes at other horizons. On equities — the headline use case — there is
  nothing. Proxy/self-prediction support and a non-robust point estimate ⇒ **WEAK**, never
  REAL (the desk's `t ≥ 2`-on-an-*independent*-tape bar is not met).
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Every conditional win-rate is *below* its base rate; the one
  "significant" gold rule loses **−1.3%/yr** net against **+11.4%/yr** buy-and-hold; the TIPS
  rule merely re-harvests autocorrelation and still trails buy-and-hold. There is no deployable,
  independent, cost-survivable edge.
- **Free macro-timing lunch? — BUSTED.** "The bond market's inflation forecast times your
  portfolio" is a **multiple-testing + self-prediction illusion**: scan two signals × three
  assets × three horizons and ~one cell lights up by luck, while the "best" `|t|` you find is
  the proxy predicting itself. The synthetic control confirms the null is real. (See the
  related [Real-Rate-Regime](../119-real-rate-regime/) and [Fed-Model](../118-fed-model/)
  rate studies for the same regress-the-macro-variable trap.)
